correctness.rationale: Direct substitution of the source parameter set confirms that the printed global comparison can reverse sign at an admissible simplex state even though the source R0 is below one. For q=S/rho-L/(1-rho), subtracting the two susceptible equations gives the exact scalar identity q' = -(mu+beta H)q -(alpha-beta)H S/rho, so the positive part contracts at least as e^{-mu t}. The exact decomposition alpha S+beta L = a0(S+L)+(alpha-beta)rho(1-rho)q then bounds the time-dependent effective susceptibility by a0 plus an exponentially decaying excess. When R0<1, after finite time the infected two-by-two Metzler block is entrywise dominated by a fixed Hurwitz Metzler matrix, which yields exponential decay of E and I; scalar variation of constants then gives R to zero and S,L to their disease-free shares. The disease-free Jacobian is locally stable at the same threshold, so global attraction plus local stability gives global asymptotic stability. A fresh independent symbolic reconstruction verified the q equation and the susceptibility decomposition; the exact package checker separately verifies those identities, the infected-block determinant, and the numerical sign-reversal counterexample.

originality.rationale: The complete Pan--Tang primary PDF was inspected through the normalized model, R0 calculation, Theorem 1 and its global-stability proof. The source explicitly uses the invalid pointwise replacement of alpha S+beta L by the disease-free weighted value. No correction or erratum giving the submitted composition variable was found in targeted searches. Related heterogeneous-susceptibility epidemic models use different flows or Lyapunov structures and do not imply this exact contraction identity. The submitted result therefore supplies a source-specific repair that preserves the published threshold rather than merely pointing out an error.
residual_risks: A very recent unindexed erratum to Pan--Tang could overlap, although targeted correction/erratum searches found none.
